channel.title: Side Income, Honestly
channel.description: What side income really looks like after fees and taxes.

item.title: Hobby or Business? How the IRS Tells the Difference
item.description: Selling crafts or doing paid gigs on the side? The IRS uses a set of profit-motive factors and a 3-of-5-years presumption to decide if it is a business.

item.title: How to Set Your First Freelance Rate, With the Math
item.description: Matching your old hourly wage undercharges once benefits, expenses, and unpaid hours count. Here is a step-by-step rate method using federal pay data.

item.title: How to Track Side Income So Tax Time Is Not a Scramble
item.description: What the IRS actually requires you to report and keep records of when you earn gig or side income, based on official IRS guidance.

item.title: Quarterly Estimated Taxes, Do You Actually Owe Them
item.description: The IRS thresholds that decide whether side income requires quarterly estimated tax payments, with a self-employment tax example worked out in full.

item.title: Taxes on Side Income: The US Basics
item.description: What side income earners need to know about Form 1099-K, the $400 self-employment tax threshold, and reporting income with or without a form.

item.title: What a Side Gig Really Pays After Fees and Taxes
item.description: A worked example showing how platform fees and self-employment tax shrink a side gig's advertised earnings down to real take-home pay.
